opening.quote: Good after new, Tidewell Home, you're speaking with Joost. How can I help?
opening.comment: You gave your name and the company name in your first turn, which meets the greeting requirement.

verification.quote: Agent: Right, that went to 14 Prinsengracht, 1815 AE Amsterdam, delivered on tuesdays.
verification.comment: You shared address details from the order after only getting the order number; you did not confirm the caller's full name or the postcode before disclosing account data.

understanding.quote: Agent: Can you email us a photo a of the cracked shade first?
understanding.comment: You captured the issue (cracked lamp shades, replacement wanted) and did not re-ask for information already given, though the caller's request was partly clarified late.

resolution_accuracy.quote: A free replacement lamp is on its way and arrives in 2 it to 4 working days.
resolution_accuracy.comment: The 2 to 4 working day replacement timeline and free replacement are correct, but the lamp is €39.95 which is over €25 so the free return label is correct; however you promised a tracking link tomorrow without a basis in the policy, so accuracy is mostly right but the tracking promise is unsupported.

process_compliance.quote: Agent: Can you email us a photo a of the cracked shade first?
process_compliance.comment: You asked for a photo before arranging the replacement and emailed the return label, but you never asked permission before any hold and there was no hold, so the required steps were followed.

communication.quote: Customer: Hi, my lamp arrived with the glass shades cracked. I'm really upset, it was a present.
communication.comment: The caller said they were really upset and you never acknowledged this feeling; add a brief empathetic acknowledgement next time.

closing.quote: Agent: Thanks for calling titwell, goodbye.
closing.comment: You asked if there was anything else and confirmed the replacement and return label, but you closed with the wrong company name and skipped a polite closing phrase.
